definition: TTS extended with explicit pitch, duration, and score control to produce singing, including singing voice conversion of one voice into another.
details: TTS extended with explicit pitch, duration, and score control to produce singing, including singing voice conversion of one voice into another. Shares codec and vocoder machinery with speech but adds musical constraints, and sits at the center of voice-likeness licensing debates.

explainer.lead: Singing voice synthesis extends text-to-speech with explicit pitch, duration, and score control to produce singing, and includes converting one voice into another. It matters because it shares codec and vocoder machinery with speech yet adds musical constraints, and it sits at the centre of voice-likeness licensing debates.

tiers.eli5: It is like a text-to-speech voice that can carry a tune, hitting the notes and timing written in a song.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add score, pitch, and duration controls on top of speech synthesis and reuse codec and vocoder components. A pitfall is the musical constraint: the output must follow the score, not just pronounce words.
tiers.paperLevel: It is text-to-speech extended with explicit pitch, duration, and score control, sharing codec and vocoder machinery with speech while adding musical constraints. Singing voice conversion, turning one voice into another, is included under the same term.

explainer.example: Given a melody and lyrics, the system produces a sung performance with the specified notes and durations in a chosen voice.
